summary: Closing the one axis never exercised so far. A new investigation asks whether a member stopped and restarted from its persisted storage recovers the committed state it missed, relearns the leader, and regains the ability to propose without diverging, and it is submitted with an experiment in the three-node Node-API cluster: commit a payload on all nodes, stop node 2, commit a second payload while it is down, rebuild node 2 from the same MemoryStorage the driver has been updating, advance the clock ten rounds with delivery between rounds so the leader issues heartbeats, then record node 2's leader, whether the missed payload appears in its applied entries and on every node, and whether a proposal from it returns and commits. Three comparisons cover recovery of the missed payload, the proposal returning instead of staying pending, and the proposal committing. A local run of the new test shows the expected behaviour: node 2 restarts with committed and applied index 2, then reports leader 1, recovers the missed payload with commit and applied index 3, and its own proposal returns with no error and commits on all three nodes. Two details are documented rather than hidden: the clock must be advanced after the restart because a restarted member otherwise receives no traffic from the leader in this harness, and storage loss, snapshot installation, simultaneous restarts and ticks during the outage are outside this scope.
